companyDescription: NASA lunar contractor & space infrastructure company · IM-3 South Pole mission H2 2026 · $1.1B backlog · Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter prime contractor — the Lockheed Martin of the new Moon race
priceNote: Dipped on $500M equity offering announced Jun 2. Core thesis intact: $1.1B backlog + $180M South Pole NASA contract + IM-3 H2 2026. Roth Capital PT $75 = 279% upside.
summary: Intuitive Machines is becoming the primary commercial contractor for NASA's lunar program. The company won a $180M NASA lunar South Pole mission contract, acquired Lanteris Space Systems for up to $851M, and became prime contractor for two NASA lunar imaging instruments. Record Q1 2026 backlog hit $1.1B (+records). IM-3 Reiner Gamma mission is planned for H2 2026. Avg analyst PT $40.78 = 106% upside — Roth Capital's $75 street-high implies 279%.

catalysts.name: IM-3 Mission Launch (H2 2026)
catalysts.description: IM-3 will land at Reiner Gamma — a magnetic anomaly near the Moon's equator. Mission is contracted and funded. Successful landing would demonstrate operational repeatability beyond IM-1 and IM-2, unlocking commercial and government launch cadence.

catalysts.name: NASA $180M South Pole Contract
catalysts.description: Intuitive Machines won a $180.4M NASA contract for a lunar South Pole mission. This is NASA's highest-priority landing zone — critical for Artemis base camp and water ice research. LUNR is the sole contractor.

catalysts.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Prime Contractor
catalysts.description: LUNR was awarded prime contractor role for NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera and ShadowCam (Korea Pathfinder). Two 3-year cost-plus contracts totaling $20M — recurring government revenue that validates LUNR as NASA's trusted commercial partner.

risks: IM-1 (Feb 2024) landed sideways — execution risk on lunar missions is real and binary (success vs. mission failure)
$500M at-the-market equity raise announced Jun 2 = dilution risk; share count could increase 15-20%
NASA budget uncertainty — US government continuing resolution or spending cuts could delay contract payouts
Small market cap ($2.5B) with high volatility — 52-week range $8 to $46 shows extreme swings
Lanteris Space Systems acquisition up to $851M = significant integration and cost risk

macroRisk.rateOutlook: FOMC July 29 — 70% hold. LUNR revenue is primarily NASA government contracts — fixed-price and cost-plus contracts are not rate-sensitive.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Space hardware costs rising with materials inflation, but cost-plus contracts pass through cost increases to NASA. Fixed-price contracts have some margin compression risk.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: LOW impact. Government contract base is rate-insensitive. Commercial launch revenue (smaller portion) is more macro-sensitive. Dilution from $500M equity raise is bigger risk than rates.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk LOW. NASA contract base provides rate-insensitive revenue. Key risks are execution (mission success) and dilution from $500M equity raise.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Space infrastructure stocks typically run 20-50% in the 4-8 weeks leading up to a confirmed mission launch date. LUNR IM-2 (Feb 2024 attempt) ran +85% in 3 weeks before launch. IM-3 confirmation date will likely trigger a similar pre-launch run.

postWin.note: LUNR IM-1 success (Feb 2024): stock ran +120% over 2 weeks as it became first US commercial lunar lander. IM-3 success at South Pole (higher strategic value) could be similar.

postLose.note: LUNR IM-1 landing failure (landed sideways) — stock dropped -35% over 1 week despite partial success. Full mission failure = -50-60% scenario.

comparableCases.event: IM-1 First Commercial US Lunar Landing
comparableCases.note: IM-1 landed sideways but still became first US commercial Moon lander. Stock +120% pre-landing, then -35% on partial failure. Shows the extreme binary nature — need full IM-3 success for sustained re-rate.
Space infrastructure peers (RKLB) re-rated +35% on major government contract wins. LUNR's $180M NASA South Pole win is similarly large relative to market cap.
Virgin Galactic first commercial spaceflight triggered +45% re-rate. Space milestone events consistently deliver outsized near-term moves — the Moon is higher stakes.
